newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-GRAF HAS LAST BIT OF BUSINESS BEFORE REUNION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF HAS LAST BIT OF BUSINESS BEFORE REUNION.

text.p: Steffi Graf has one last tennis stop before returning to Germany for a rousing reunion with her father -- the season-ending WTA Tour Chase Championships, where the 27-year-old world number one defends her title.

Graf, who produced an extraordinary year of tennis despite the emotional upheaval wrought by her father Peter's 15-month incarceration over tax evasion charges, could be forgiven if her mind is not entirely on her game at Madison Square Garden.
"I can't wait to get back to Germany when the Masters (WTA championship) is over," Graf said from her warm-up event in Philadelphia after hearing of her father's release on bail on Friday.
"I have hardly been able to sleep the last few nights but I hope that is all over now," she said.
The top-seeded Graf will need to maintain her formidable focus one last time if she is to crown a season that has seen her win the French, Wimbledon and U.S. Open championships.
The leading 16 points winners on the WTA Tour gather for the $2 million season finale starting on Monday, all hoping to end their season on a high note.
While Graf will enter the famous arena by stepping over the Madison Square Garden Walk of Fame where she was honoured earlier this month, her rivals have more to prove.

Second seed Monica Seles hopes to rebound from a pair of poor performances to challenge for the number one ranking. Arantxa Sanchez Vicario is eager to shed her bridesmaid image, and rising star Martina Hingis aims for her first big title.
Seles, struggling to overcome the affects of a sore left serving shoulder, is coming off straight-set losses to Jennifer Capriati in Chicago and Hingis in Oakland.
"It would definitely be nice to end the year off well at the Chase Championships," said Seles, who won the Australian Open to start the year and was runner-up to Graf at the U.S. Open.
Sanchez, ranked co-number two in the world with Seles, was runner-up in the season's other three Grand Slams.
"It's the last tournament of the year so, of course, you want to do well," said Sanchez, who also sees it as a springboard. "It is also preparation for going to next year. I look at it both ways."

Hingis is riding high, enjoying a number six ranking after drubbing Seles 6-2 6-0 in the Oakland final. The 16-year-old Swiss, who reached the U.S. Open semifinals before falling to Graf, would get a re-match against Seles if both survive their first-round tests.

The field also includes Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport, the eighth seed, fourth-seeded former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez and sixth seed Anke Huber, who lost to compatriot Graf 6-1 2-6 6-1 4-6 6-3 in last year's title match -- the only women's event to feature a best-of-five set final.
Other top 10 players include Jana Novotna, Iva Majoli, Brenda Schultz McCarthy and Kimiko Date.
Date, Japan's greatest player, has announced her retirement at the end of the season and will be honoured at the Garden on Tuesday. She drew Seles as her first-round opponent.
Argentina's Gabriela Sabatini, a former winner of this championship who has also announced her retirement, will be honoured on Monday night.
